Problem 1

The given equation is

(64)Cdvdt=k(v−vr)(v−vt)−u+Idudt=b(v−vr)−u

Let v¯=V(v−vr),u¯=Uu, then

(65)dv¯dt=Vdvdtdu¯dt=Ududt

Plug it into the original equation, we have

(66)CVdv¯dt=kVv¯(v¯V+vr−vt)−u¯U+Idu¯dt=UbVv¯−u¯

Hence

(67)dv¯dt=kCv¯(v¯V+vr−vt)−VUCu¯+VICdu¯dt=UbVv¯−u¯

Let V=kC,U=kC2, α=k(vr−vt)C,β=bC,δ=kIC2, then the equations are transformed into

(68)dv¯dt=v¯2+αv¯−u¯+δdu¯dt=βv¯−u¯

which is desired. Note that V,U,β,δ are none-zero since C,I,vr,vt,k,b are non-zero. But α may be zero.

Problem 2

Set α=1 (and re-denote v¯ as v, u¯ as u), the system becomes

(69)dvdt=v2+v−u+δdudt=βv−u

(a) Rewrite the system into matrix form

(70)ddt[uv]=[v2+v−u+δβv−u]=[f1(u,v)f2(u,v)]=F(u,v)

At the critical points, we have

(71)ddt[uv]=0,{v2+v−u+δ=0βv−u=0⇒{u=β2(β−1−s),v=12(β−1−s)u=β2(β−1+s),v=12(β−1+s)

where s2=(1−β)2−4δ. The Jacobi matrix at (u,v) is

(72)J(u,v)=∇F(u,v)=[∂f1∂u∂f1∂v∂f2∂u∂f2∂v]=[−12v+1−1β]

which contains no u. Fix v, we can find the eigenvalues of it at (u,v)

(73)|J(u,v)−λI|=|−1−λ2v+1−1β−λ|=0⇒{λ1=12(−1+β−t)λ2=12(−1+β+t)

where t2=(β−1)(β+3)−8v=(1−β)2±4s. Therefore,

  1. If (1−β)2<4δ, then s2<0, (8) has no solutions. I.e. there's no critical point.

  2. If (1−β)2=4δ, then s=0, (8) has only one solution (critical point)

    (74)(u,v)=(β(β−1)2,β−12)

    at this critical point, t2=(1−β)2⩾0 , hence λ1, λ2 are both real.

    • If β=1, then δ=0, λ1=λ2=0, the critical point (11) is an unstable saddle point.

    • If β>1, then λ1>0,λ2=0, the critical point (11) is an unstable source.

    • If β<1, then λ1<0,λ2=0, the critical point (11) is an unstable saddle point referring to the graph below:

  3. If (1−β)2>4δ, then s2>0, s has 2 values, one positive and one negative, (8) has 2 distinct solutions (critical points)

    (75)P1=(u1,v1)=(β2(β−1−(1−β)2−4δ),12(β−1−(1−β)2−4δ))P2=(u2,v2)=(β2(β−1+(1−β)2−4δ),12(β−1+(1−β)2−4δ))

    • At P1, t2=(1−β)2+4s=(1−β)2+4(1−β)2−4δ>0, therefore about P1, we know that

      • λ1⩽0, '=' holds iff β=2,δ=14

      • λ2⩾0, '=' holds iff β=0,δ=14

      Since (1−β)2>4δ as we assumed, λ1<0, λ2>0 always holds at P1, that is, P1 is an unstable saddle point.

    • At P2, t2=(1−β)2−4s=(1−β)2−4(1−β)2−4δ, let

      (76)m=164(15−28β+10β2+4β3−β4)

      therefore about P1, we know that

      1. When δ=m, t=0, there's λ1=λ2=β−12

        • If β>1, then λ1,λ2>0, P2 is an unstable source

        • If β<1, then λ1,λ2<0, P2 is a stable sink

      2. When δ<m,t2<0, there's λ1,λ2∈C,

        • If β>1, then Re λ1,Re λ2>0, P2 is an unstable spiral

        • If β<1, then Re λ1,Re λ2<0, P2 is a stable spiral

        • If β=1, then Re λ1=Re λ2=0,Im λ1,Im λ2≠0, P2 is a stable center,

      3. When δ>m,t2>0, there's λ1,λ∈R,

        • If β>1 and m⩽δ<(1−β)24, −1+β+t>−1+β−t>0, i.e. λ2>λ1>0, P2 is an unstable source

        • If β<1 and m⩽δ<(1−β)24, −1+β−t<−1+β+t<0, i.e. λ1<λ2<0, P2 is a stable sink.

        • If β=1, as m=0, 0=m⩽δ<(1−β)24=0 never holds.

(b) Set β=2, the equation becomes

(77)ddt[uv]=[v2+v−u+δ2v−u]=[f1(u,v)f2(u,v)]=F(u,v)

If furtherly δ=0, referring to the debate in (a), since (1−β)2>4δ, there're 2 critical points P1=(0,0),P2=(2,1), and at P1, λ1<0,λ2>0, P1 is an unstable saddle point.

Besides, when β=2, we get s2=1−4δ, t2=1±4s, m=1564. Referring to the debate above in (a),

  • when δ>14, there's no critical points

  • when δ=14, there's only one unstable source critical point.

  • when δ<14, there're 2 critical points, one is an unstable saddle point, and the other one is,

    • if 1564⩽δ<14, is an unstable source

    • if δ<1564, is and unstable spiral.

By (12),

(78)P1=(u1,v1)=(1−1−4δ,12(1−1−4δ))P2=(u2,v2)=(1+1−4δ,12(1+1−4δ))

as δ increases, u1↑, u2↓, u2>u1, v1↑, v2↓, v2>v1,

(c) If there is limit cycles, then there could be some δ,β, making the eigenvalues of the Jacobi at the center of the trajectory purely imaginary (sufficient condition). Thus, by the debate above, we must have β=1 and t2=(1−β)2±s=±s<0. To make critical point exist, we must have δ<0.

  • Assume β=1,δ<0, by the debate above, P2 is a stable center, hence there exists infinite limit cycles around it.

  • When β≠1, as

    (79)∂f1∂u+∂f2∂v=−1+β≠0,∀ (u,v)∈R2

    Applying Bendixson's Criterion, the system has no closed trajectories inside R2.

  • When β=1,δ⩾0, there's either no critical point, or only one saddle point. Since the index of a saddle is −1 and that of a closed orbit is 1, there exist no limit cycles.

    In summary, we can conclude that limit cycles exist if and only if β=1 and δ<0.

    The following graph shows the existence of a limit cycle when β=1, δ=−1:

(d) To produce homoclinic orbits, we'd better produce saddle point first. By (c), when β=1,δ<0, there appears a center P2 and a saddle point P1, note that the trajectory emitted from P1, hence there exists homoclinic orbits for the same parameter values.

(e) The bifurcation occurs when 14(1−β)2=δ, and at this time, the critical point

(80)u=β2(β−1),v=u=12(β−1)

Hence the parametric expression of the curve of the points where bifurcation occurs should be

(81)Cu(β)=(14(1−β)2,β(β−1)2),Cv(β)=(14(1−β)2,β−12)

If we put it onto the uv plane, then the expression is

(82)C(β)=(β(β−1)2,β−12)

When β<1, P2 is stable, otherwise, it's unstable.

Question

I chose 2 sets of parameters which produce distinct behaviors:

one is the only parameter region in which a stable center appears. i.e. β=1,δ<0. The corresponding phase plane, by the debate above, contains a saddle point in the third quadrant, coordinates at (−−δ,−−δ), and a center, coordinated at (−δ,−δ), they're symmetric about the origin. See the animation below:

At δ=0, the 2 critical point will merge to a single one, and the limit cycles (closed trajectories) will disappear. As δ exceed 0, those critical point will disappear as well. Near the saddle, we can calculate out the eigenvectors of its linearized expression. For example, when δ=−4, the saddle is (−2,−2) the Jacobi matrix is

(83)J(−2,−2)=[−1−3−11],λ1=−1,v1=(3,1)T,λ2=2,v2=(−1,1)T

Hence along the line (−2,−2)+μ(3,1), the trajectories will converge to (−2,−2) but along the line (−2,−2)+(−1,1), the trajectories will diverge.

Also, at the other critical point (center) (2,2), the Jacobi matrix is

(84)J(2,2)=[−15−11],λ1=2i,v1=(1−2i,1)T,λ2=−2i,v2=(1+2i,1)T

Hence the trajectories around (2,2) is clockwise.

This behavior indicates that when b=C (membrane capacitance), if we set the initial membrane potential and recovery current near 2, they will oscillate of the same range of amplitude and never reach steady state.

The other is the region that no stable critical point exists. i.e β>1. When |u| is large enough, we can find that v′(t)=v2+v−u+δ is small, hence the change of recovery current will be small, thus the trajectories will be more horizontal.

At this time, there're at most 2 (or 1 or none) unstable critical points, one is unstable saddle, the other is an unstable source or unstable spiral. For example, when β=3,δ=0, The critical point in the first quadrate is (6,2) and the Jacobi matrix is

(85)J(2,2)=[−15−13],λ1=1+i,v1=(2−i,1)T,λ2=1−i,v2=(2+i,1)T

Thus the spiral is clockwise and unstable. All trajectories will diverge to the far right.

This behavior indicates that when b>C (membrane capacitance), any initial membrane potential and recovery current will result in the destruct of the cell neutron (surely exactly on the critical point will prevent this, but any small perturbation will result in this). The steady-state of the neutron cannot be recovered anymore.
